why: Because `else return -1` sits inside the loop, the method returns on the first pass, so it checks only arr[0] and never looks for the last occurrence. This treats the loop as a single check, which is the ForIsConditional misconception.

concepts.quote: for (...) { if (arr[i] == key) return i; else return -1; }
concepts.why: Both branches return, so the body runs at most once and the loop never reaches the later elements.

concepts.quote: if (arr[i] == key) return i; else return -1;
concepts.why: The two-way choice is written correctly, but it is used wrongly: the 'not found' result is decided after a single comparison.
It correctly uses arr[i] for the element and returns i as the position, but goes no further.
A correct comparison expression, but there is no reasoning about how it is evaluated.
